answer: Ask what breaks first, and it is the accounting: price one unit of work at the hours it takes to reproduce, then dilute the payout whenever peers disagree and forbid grading your own recruit, so a copied answer returns a fraction of a fraction. A comet sighting, an orchard spray log and a forge heat run each cost about an hour. A farm pays that hour per clone and collects the diluted share only if unrelated graders agree.
